summary: Python modules should wrap execution in a main function called under if __name__ == '__main__' so they can be imported in unit tests.
questions: Why should my module have a main() guarded by __name__?

answer_card.title: Use a main() function
answer_card.answer_md:
Wrap execution in `main()` and call it conditionally so unit tests can import the module:
```python
if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
